verdict.rationale: Yubico's own python-fido2 library documents verifying attestation signatures. PIV attestation docs describe a certificate proving a key was generated on the device, so the core of verifying genuine-device attestation at registration is covered. However, nothing documents enforcing an allowlist of approved key models, such as AAGUID or metadata checks, at enrollment. Missing for 10: documented model/AAGUID allowlist enforcement at registration, FIDO metadata or attestation-root verification guidance, attestation policy in the WebAuthn server library, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a security engineer, I can verify device attestation at registration to enforce that only genuine, approved key models are enrolled

citations.quote: Provides library functionality for communicating with a FIDO device over USB as well as verifying attestation and assertion signatures.
The concept of attestation is used to show that a certain asymmetric key has been generated on device and not imported.
This certificate should be used for the purpose of verifying that the key was generated in device.
